chasm city.title: Chasm City
chasm city.author: Alastair Reynolds
chasm city.why: A man hunts a killer across a ruined future city and through a strange past; dark, rich space opera readers praise.

upgrade.title: Upgrade
upgrade.author: Blake Crouch
upgrade.why: Comments are lukewarm, one calling it boring.

hate u give.title: The Hate U Give
hate u give.author: Angie Thomas
hate u give.why: A teenage girl speaks up after a police shooting of her friend; a moving YA that changed readers' views.

negative space.title: Negative Space
negative space.author: B.R. Yeager
negative space.why: A cosmic-horror novel about despair and obsession; readers call it the bleakest book they know, yet brilliant.

rainbow.title: The Rainbow
rainbow.author: D. H. Lawrence
rainbow.why: Readers mention disliking it or confuse it with another book.

nuclear war.title: Nuclear War
nuclear war.author: Annie Jacobsen
nuclear war.why: A minute-by-minute account of how a nuclear war would unfold; fascinating and terrifying.

falling free.title: Falling Free
falling free.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
falling free.why: A engineer defends genetically engineered workers fighting for freedom; a standalone Vorkosigan-universe novel, though not the best starting point.

long way down.title: Long Way Down
long way down.author: Jason Reynolds
long way down.why: A teen rides an elevator down while deciding whether to avenge his brother; a quick novel in verse praised for its form.

eighth life.title: The Eighth Life
eighth life.author: Nino Haratischwili
eighth life.why: Eight generations of one Georgian family across the twentieth century; a huge book readers could not stop reading.

chosen.title: The Chosen
chosen.author: Chaim Potok
chosen.why: Two Jewish boys in 1940s Brooklyn form an unlikely friendship; an all-time favourite for many.

echopraxia.title: Echopraxia
echopraxia.author: Peter Watts
echopraxia.why: A hard-science sequel to Blindsight about post-human minds; hugely ambitious, though some readers cannot engage.

new york trilogy.title: The New York Trilogy
new york trilogy.author: Paul Auster
new york trilogy.why: Three metaphysical detective stories in New York; readers find it weird and unforgettable.

poisoners handbook.title: The Poisoner's Handbook
poisoners handbook.author: Deborah Blum
poisoners handbook.why: The rise of forensic science through Jazz Age poison cases; engrossing history and chemistry.

sheltering sky.title: The Sheltering Sky
sheltering sky.author: Paul Bowles
sheltering sky.why: An American couple unravels in the Sahara; a dark, haunting classic.

lilith.title: Lilith
lilith.author: George MacDonald
lilith.why: A Victorian visionary fantasy about a library and a dreamlike other world; admired by C. S. Lewis.

bfg.title: The BFG
bfg.author: Roald Dahl
bfg.why: A girl befriends a gentle giant who blows dreams; a beloved Roald Dahl favourite.

deerskin.title: Deerskin
deerskin.author: Robin McKinley
deerskin.why: A dark retelling of the Donkeyskin fairy tale about surviving abuse; strong but with serious content warnings.

bury my heart at wounded knee.title: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
bury my heart at wounded knee.author: Dee Alexander Brown
bury my heart at wounded knee.why: The destruction of Native American nations told from their side; recommended as history that brings the past to life.

fool.title: Fool
fool.author: Christopher Moore
fool.why: King Lear retold through the court jester with plenty of bawdy jokes; readers rank it near Lamb.

running man.title: The Running Man
running man.author: Stephen King
running man.why: A desperate man joins a lethal TV game show in a dystopian future; a quick, punchy Bachman novel.

restaurant at the end of the universe.title: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe
restaurant at the end of the universe.author: Douglas Adams
restaurant at the end of the universe.why: The second Hitchhiker's Guide book sends its heroes further across a ridiculous galaxy.

nightwood.title: Nightwood
nightwood.author: Djuna Barnes
nightwood.why: A strange modernist novel about love and ruin among Paris expatriates; confounding but rewarding.

zeitoun.title: Zeitoun
zeitoun.author: Dave Eggers
zeitoun.why: A Syrian-American man trapped in New Orleans after Katrina; a gripping true story readers recommend.

game.title: The Game
game.author: Neil Strauss
game.why: Comments refer to other books with the same title.

siddartha.title: Siddhartha
siddartha.author: Hermann Hesse
siddartha.why: A man's search for spiritual enlightenment in ancient India; a short book readers return to.

absolutely true diary of a part time ind.title: The Absolutely True Diary of a Part-Time Indian
absolutely true diary of a part time ind.author: Sherman Alexie
absolutely true diary of a part time ind.why: A boy leaves his reservation school for a white high school; funny and honest.

simple plan.title: A Simple Plan
simple plan.author: Scott Smith
simple plan.why: Three men keep a stash of cash and spiral into paranoia; so intense readers need breaks.

chlorine.title: Chlorine
chlorine.author: Jade Song
chlorine.why: A competitive swimmer's obsession turns into body horror; best read as literary fiction.

books of the raksura.title: The Cloud Roads (Books of the Raksura)
books of the raksura.author: Martha Wells
books of the raksura.why: Shapeshifting winged people and a lost outcast in a rich fantasy world; recommended for fresh worldbuilding.

summer of night.title: Summer of night
summer of night.author: Dan Simmons
summer of night.why: Kids in 1960 small-town Illinois confront an ancient evil; nostalgic coming-of-age horror.

alls well.title: All's Well
alls well.author: Mona Awad
alls well.why: A theatre director in pain gets a strange bargain in a surreal, disorienting novel readers love for its weirdness.

snuff.title: Snuff
snuff.author: Chuck Palahniuk
snuff.why: A porn-star record attempt narrated by several voices; a wild ride for Palahniuk fans.

phantom of the opera.title: The Phantom of the Opera
phantom of the opera.author: Gaston Leroux
phantom of the opera.why: A disfigured genius haunts the Paris Opera; a gothic romance about unrequited love.

dream count.title: Dream Count
dream count.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
dream count.why: Four women's lives in a time of pandemic; chosen by a book club.

iron dream.title: The Iron Dream
iron dream.author: Norman Spinrad
iron dream.why: A novel supposedly written by an exiled Hitler; a clever and funny satire of fascist fantasy.

bluebeard.title: Bluebeard
bluebeard.author: Kurt Vonnegut
bluebeard.why: An aging painter recalls his life and art; one of Vonnegut's favourite late novels.

last days.title: Last Days
last days.author: Brian Evenson
last days.why: A detective investigates a cult leader's murder in a bizarre, brutal tale; weird and brilliant.

last murder at the end of the world.title: The Last Murder at the End of the World
last murder at the end of the world.author: Stuart Turton
last murder at the end of the world.why: A murder mystery in the last human village; clever but divisive.

big rock candy mountain.title: The Big Rock Candy Mountain
big rock candy mountain.author: Wallace Stegner
big rock candy mountain.why: A family chases dreams across the American West; praised as a semi-autobiographical saga.

notes on an execution.title: Notes on an Execution
notes on an execution.author: Danya Kukafka
notes on an execution.why: A serial killer's final hours told through the women around him; a top read for many.

red and the black.title: The Red and the Black
red and the black.author: Stendhal
red and the black.why: A young man's ambitions rise and fall in post-Napoleonic France; a classic of ambition.

dealing with dragons.title: Dealing with Dragons
dealing with dragons.author: Patricia C. Wrede
dealing with dragons.why: A princess runs off to be a dragon's helper; a witty fairy tale spoof.

different seasons.title: Different Seasons
different seasons.author: Stephen King
different seasons.why: Four King novellas including the basis for The Shawshank Redemption; readers love all of them.

night film.title: Night Film
night film.author: Marisha Pessl
night film.why: A journalist digs into the death of a reclusive horror director's daughter; creepy and absorbing.

days at the morisaki bookshop.title: Days at the Morisaki Bookshop
days at the morisaki bookshop.author: Satoshi Yagisawa
days at the morisaki bookshop.why: A heartbroken young woman finds comfort in her uncle's Tokyo secondhand bookshop; a short, gentle read.

robot.title: I, Robot
robot.author: Isaac Asimov
robot.why: Comments are about Monk and Robot, not this book.

palimpsest.title: Palimpsest
palimpsest.author: Catherynne M. Valente
palimpsest.why: A sexually transmitted dream city draws lost people; delightfully unhinged, Mieville-like.

strange houses.title: Strange Houses
strange houses.author: Uketsu
strange houses.why: A mystery and horror story solved through floor plans; so quick that readers finish it in one sitting.

let them theory.title: The Let Them Theory
let them theory.author: Mel Robbins
let them theory.why: A self-help book about letting others be themselves and focusing on yourself; readers say it shifted their perspective.

children of men.title: The Children of Men
children of men.author: P. D. James
children of men.why: A world with no births awaits its final generation; a literary dystopia.

run.title: Run
run.author: Blake Crouch
run.why: A society falls apart in a terrifying chase thriller; split opinions, but some read it in one sitting.

no exit.title: No Exit
no exit.author: Taylor Adams
no exit.why: A stranded student finds a kidnapped child in a snowed-in rest stop; a fast thriller.

street.title: The Street
street.author: Ann Petry
street.why: A Black single mother struggles against poverty in 1940s Harlem; recommended for its power.

sun does shine.title: The sun does shine
sun does shine.author: Anthony Ray Hinton
sun does shine.why: A man wrongfully condemned spends 30 years on death row; a moving story of survival.

bloodchild.title: Bloodchild
bloodchild.author: Octavia E. Butler
bloodchild.why: A short story about a human boy and an alien host; widely recommended for its unsettling beauty.

ivanhoe.title: Ivanhoe
ivanhoe.author: Walter Scott
ivanhoe.why: Knights, outlaws and rivalry in medieval England; an adventure classic with archaic language.

fall or dodge in hell.title: Fall; or, Dodge in Hell
fall or dodge in hell.author: Neal Stephenson
fall or dodge in hell.why: Digital afterlife and mind uploading played out over generations; ambitious but weaker than his best.

hard rain falling.title: Hard rain falling
hard rain falling.author: Don Carpenter
hard rain falling.why: A grim, compelling story of a young man's life in jails and on the margins; one of the best ones for some readers.

dharma bums.title: The Dharma Bums
dharma bums.author: Jack Kerouac
dharma bums.why: Kerouac's story of mountains and Buddhism with Beat friends; good for self-discovery.

drivers seat.title: The Driver's Seat
drivers seat.author: Muriel Spark
drivers seat.why: A woman on a strange trip heading towards a shocking end; short, odd and easy to read.

gales of november.title: The Gales of November
gales of november.author: John U. Bacon
gales of november.why: The sinking of the Edmund Fitzgerald on Lake Superior; recommended for its gripping detail.

casual vacancy.title: The Casual Vacancy
casual vacancy.author: J. K. Rowling
casual vacancy.why: A small English village erupts after a councillor dies; depressing but overlooked.

copenhagen trilogy.title: The Copenhagen Trilogy
copenhagen trilogy.author: Tove Ditlevsen
copenhagen trilogy.why: Tove Ditlevsen's three memoirs from childhood to addiction; stunning if not joyful.

stars are legion.title: The Stars Are Legion
stars are legion.author: Kameron Hurley
stars are legion.why: Women fight for control of a living world-ship; imaginative and gnarly.

art of fielding.title: The Art of Fielding
art of fielding.author: Chad Harbach
art of fielding.why: A talented baseball shortstop loses his confidence at a college; liked by many, though a few found it only so-so.

space merchants.title: The Space Merchants
space merchants.author: Frederik Pohl
space merchants.why: A copywriter in a corporate-ruled world is plunged into intrigue; a prescient dystopia.

tiger.title: The Tiger
tiger.author: John Vaillant
tiger.why: A hunt for a man-eating tiger in the Russian Far East; far more than an animal story.

wasp.title: Wasp
wasp.author: Eric Frank Russell
wasp.why: One man waging a guerrilla war on an enemy planet; darkly funny and clever.

her body and other parties.title: Her Body and Other Parties
her body and other parties.author: Carmen Maria Machado
her body and other parties.why: Surreal, queer stories about women's bodies; recommended collection.
